scenarios.name: S1: Parse DICOM files and create schema
scenarios.input: I have 500 DICOM CT scan files in /data/dicom_scans. Parse the metadata and create the Snowflake schema for our radiology department.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Router detects PARSE intent, loads dicom-parser/SKILL.md. Skill runs Step 1 (--analyze-only) to inventory files, STOPS for confirmation, then Step 2 creates 19 tables from references/data_model_ddl.sql, Step 3 parses with --snowflake --validate --quality-score, Step 4 runs validation_queries.sql.
scenarios.actual_output_summary: TRACE: (1) Router Environment Config fires — detects current context, asks user for {database}/{schema}/{warehouse}. STOPS. (2) User confirms. (3) Intent detection matches 'parse DICOM' + 'DICOM to Snowflake' triggers → PARSE. (4) Loads dicom-parser/SKILL.md. (5) Step 1: runs `python scripts/parse_dicom.py ./data/dicom_scans --recursive --analyze-only` — outputs file count by modality, date ranges, equipment. STOPS for confirmation. (6) Step 2: reads references/data_model_ddl.sql, substitutes {database}.{schema}, executes 19 CREATE TABLE DDLs. STOPS to show `SHOW TABLES`. (7) Step 3: `python scripts/parse_dicom.py ./data/dicom_scans --recursive --snowflake --database {database} --schema {schema} --validate --quality-score`. (8) Step 4: runs validation_queries.sql. STOPS to present results. All stopping points enforced. All placeholders substituted. No hardcoded values. No hallucinated tools or commands.
scenarios.notes: Workflow is fully traceable. 4 stopping points hit as specified. pydicom parser flags (--analyze-only, --validate, --quality-score) all documented. DDL references data_model_ddl.sql with 19 tables including RADIOLOGY_REPORTS. No missing entities.

scenarios.name: S2: Set up cascading Dynamic Table ingestion pipeline
scenarios.input: We need a continuous ingestion pipeline for DICOM data arriving from our PACS system. Use Dynamic Tables for cascading normalization from raw JSON.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Router detects INGEST intent, loads dicom-ingestion/SKILL.md. Step 1 presents 4 patterns, user selects Cascading DTs (#2). Step 2 creates stage/formats, Step 3 creates DICOM_RAW, Step 4 creates 5+1 cascading DTs from references/cascading_dynamic_tables.sql, Step 9 creates validation summary DT.
scenarios.actual_output_summary: TRACE: (1) Router env config → {database}/{schema}/{warehouse} confirmed. (2) Intent: 'ingest DICOM' + 'dynamic table imaging' → INGEST. (3) Loads dicom-ingestion/SKILL.md. (4) Step 1: presents 4-option ingestion pattern menu. User selects '2. Cascading DTs'. STOPS. (5) Step 2: reads references/stage_and_raw.sql, creates DICOM_STAGE (internal), DICOM_JSON_FORMAT, DICOM_CSV_FORMAT — all fully qualified with {database}.{schema}. (6) Step 3: creates DICOM_RAW with CHANGE_TRACKING=TRUE, runs COPY INTO. STOPS to verify row counts. (7) Step 4: reads references/cascading_dynamic_tables.sql. Creates 5 DTs: DT_DICOM_PATIENTS (L1, 10min), DT_DICOM_STUDIES (L2, 10min), DT_DICOM_SERIES (L3, 10min), DT_DICOM_INSTANCES (L4, 10min), DT_DICOM_EQUIPMENT (L3, 30min). CASCADE verified: each DT joins upstream DT. STOPS to verify refresh states via INFORMATION_SCHEMA.DYNAMIC_TABLES(). (8) Step 9: creates DT_DICOM_VALIDATION_SUMMARY (30min) from same file. STOPS. All objects fully qualified. WAREHOUSE={warehouse} on all DTs.
scenarios.notes: Cascade dependency chain is correct: RAW→PATIENTS→STUDIES→SERIES→{INSTANCES,EQUIPMENT}. All DTs use LEFT JOIN to upstream DTs. TRY_TO_DATE/TRY_TO_NUMBER used for safe type casts from VARIANT. HASH() surrogate keys with GROUP BY deduplication. Validation DT cross-checks orphan counts. One minor observation: DT_DICOM_INSTANCES references r.FILE_PATH which comes from DICOM_RAW — this column name should be validated against actual DICOM_RAW DDL (stage_and_raw.sql defines it as FILE_PATH, so this is correct).

scenarios.name: S3: Build Cortex Search + Semantic View + Agent for conversational imaging analytics
scenarios.input: I want our radiologists to be able to ask natural language questions about our imaging data. Set up a conversational agent that can query our DICOM tables and search radiology reports.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Router detects AGENT intent. Checks prerequisites (Semantic View + Search Service). Routes to dicom-analytics Steps 7-9 + loads cortex-agent skill. Creates IMAGING_SEARCH_CORPUS, IMAGING_SEARCH_SVC, DICOM_ANALYTICS_SV, IMAGING_ANALYTICS_AGENT.
scenarios.actual_output_summary: TRACE: (1) Router env config. (2) Intent: 'natural language questions' + 'conversational agent' + 'query DICOM tables' + 'search radiology reports' → AGENT. (3) AGENT Routing check: prerequisites — DICOM_ANALYTICS_SV (Semantic View) and IMAGING_SEARCH_SVC (Cortex Search). If missing → route to ANALYTICS first (Steps 7-8). If exist → proceed. (4) Assume prerequisites missing — loads dicom-analytics/SKILL.md. (5) Step 7: reads references/cortex_services.sql. Creates IMAGING_SEARCH_CORPUS (denormalized join: STUDY→PATIENT→SERIES→EQUIPMENT→RADIOLOGY_REPORTS). Creates IMAGING_SEARCH_SVC (Cortex Search on SEARCH_TEXT, ATTRIBUTES: MODALITY, BODY_PART_EXAMINED, INSTITUTION_NAME, TARGET_LAG=1hr). STOPS — continuous service cost. (6) Step 8: creates DICOM_ANALYTICS_SV (Semantic View over DICOM_STUDY, DICOM_SERIES, DICOM_PATIENT, DICOM_EQUIPMENT). FACTS: NUMBER_OF_SERIES, NUMBER_OF_INSTANCES. DIMENSIONS: 15 columns. Verify with DESCRIBE SEMANTIC VIEW. STOPS. (7) Step 9: creates IMAGING_ANALYTICS_AGENT using CREATE AGENT FROM SPECIFICATION $$ YAML. Two tools: ImagingAnalyst (cortex_analyst_text_to_sql → DICOM_ANALYTICS_SV), ReportSearch (cortex_search → IMAGING_SEARCH_SVC). Model: claude-4-sonnet. STOPS — capstone integration. (8) Loads cortex-agent skill for best practices. All SQL fully qualified. Placeholder {database}.{schema} and {warehouse} substituted in Cortex Agent spec YAML.
scenarios.notes: Prerequisite check logic is sound — router checks for SV + Search Service existence before routing to AGENT. If missing, cascades to ANALYTICS first. Agent YAML spec uses correct syntax: CREATE AGENT ... FROM SPECIFICATION $$ ... $$. Tool types (cortex_analyst_text_to_sql, cortex_search) are valid Snowflake Cortex Agent tool types. Search corpus join path is correct. Semantic View FACTS/DIMENSIONS syntax is correct. One observation: Agent spec references 'claude-4-sonnet' model — this should be validated against available models at runtime but is reasonable as a placeholder.

scenarios.name: S4: Apply HIPAA governance with PHI masking and de-identification
scenarios.input: We need HIPAA compliance for our DICOM imaging tables. Apply PHI masking, create a de-identified dataset for researchers, and set up audit trails.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Router detects GOVERNANCE intent, loads imaging-governance/SKILL.md. PHI Column Inventory presented, then Steps 1-9 covering classification, tagging, masking (4 data types), RAPs, aggregation, de-identification DT, audit, retention.
scenarios.actual_output_summary: TRACE: (1) Router env config. (2) Intent: 'HIPAA' + 'PHI masking' + 'de-identification' + 'audit' → GOVERNANCE. (3) Loads imaging-governance/SKILL.md. (4) PHI Column Inventory: presents 13-row table (DICOM_PATIENT×3, DICOM_STUDY×2, DICOM_EQUIPMENT×2, DICOM_PROCEDURE_STEP×1, DICOM_FILE_LOCATION×1, DICOM_RAW×1, RADIOLOGY_REPORTS×3). Column names match DDL: patient_name, patient_id, patient_birth_date, referring_physician, accession_number, device_serial_number, station_name, performing_physician, storage_uri, metadata, patient_id, radiologist_name, report_text. STOPS. (5) Step 1: SYSTEM$CLASSIFY with auto_tag=true on PHI tables. Cross-ref with inventory. (6) Step 2: reads references/policies_and_tags.sql. Creates 3 tags (PHI_TYPE, SENSITIVITY_LEVEL, HIPAA_SAFE_HARBOR). Applies to all 13 PHI columns. Verify with TAG_REFERENCES_ALL_COLUMNS. STOPS. (7) Step 3: Creates 4 masking policies (PHI_STRING_MASK, PHI_DATE_MASK, PHI_NUMBER_MASK, PHI_VARIANT_MASK). Applies: STRING mask to 9 columns (patient_name, patient_id, referring_physician, accession_number, device_serial_number, station_name, performing_physician, storage_uri, radiologist_name, report_text — 10 actual), DATE mask to patient_birth_date, VARIANT mask to metadata. STOPS for verification. (8) Step 4: VARIANT masking details — OBJECT_DELETE chains for 12 PHI DICOM tag names. (9) Step 5: creates 3 RAPs (institution, department, consent). Consent requires PATIENT_CONSENT_REGISTRY table. STOPS. (10) Step 6: aggregation policy IMAGING_MIN_CELL_SIZE on DICOM_STUDY, DICOM_PATIENT, RADIOLOGY_REPORTS. (11) Step 7: reads references/audit_deidentification_retention.sql. Creates DICOM_STUDIES_DEIDENTIFIED DT — joins STUDY→PATIENT→SERIES→EQUIPMENT→PROCEDURE_STEP→INSTANCE→FILE_LOCATION. SHA2 hashes for UIDs/PHI, DATE_FROM_PARTS for dates, REGEXP_REPLACE for file URIs. STOPS for PHI leak validation. (12) Step 8: audit view V_PHI_ACCESS_AUDIT + PHI_ANOMALOUS_ACCESS_ALERT (4hr/100 threshold). (13) Step 9: retention — DATA_RETENTION_TIME_IN_DAYS=90, DATA_RETENTION_REGISTRY, ARCHIVE_EXPIRED_STUDIES task (monthly, 6-year cutoff). STOPS.
scenarios.notes: PHI inventory is comprehensive and all column names match current DDL (storage_uri, metadata, performing_physician — all validated in Round 2 fixes). De-identification DT join path is correct: STUDY→PATIENT, STUDY→SERIES→EQUIPMENT, STUDY→PROCEDURE_STEP, SERIES→INSTANCE→FILE_LOCATION. QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() handles series dedup. Masking policy authorized roles (PHI_AUTHORIZED, IMAGING_ADMIN) are consistent across all 4 policies. All objects fully qualified. No hallucinated columns.

scenarios.name: S5: Train imaging complexity classifier and deploy inference DT
scenarios.input: I want to build a model that predicts whether an imaging study is complex based on its DICOM metadata. Train it and set up continuous inference as a Dynamic Table.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Router detects ML intent, loads imaging-ml/SKILL.md. Steps 1-6 covering feature engineering, model training (RandomForest), registry, and inference DT.
scenarios.actual_output_summary: TRACE: (1) Router env config. (2) Intent: 'imaging model' + 'train imaging' → ML. (3) Loads imaging-ml/SKILL.md. (4) Step 1: asks user which ML task — user picks (1) Classification. STOPS. (5) Creates V_IMAGING_ML_FEATURES view: joins DICOM_STUDY→PATIENT→SERIES→EQUIPMENT. Features: NUMBER_OF_SERIES, NUMBER_OF_INSTANCES, patient_age_at_study, study_complexity_score (custom formula), is_complex_study (binary target), study_day_of_week, study_hour, is_off_hours. QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() for one-row-per-study dedup. All tables fully qualified with {database}.{schema}. Join path: STUDY→PATIENT via PATIENT_KEY, STUDY→SERIES via STUDY_KEY, SERIES→EQUIPMENT via SERIES_KEY (LEFT JOIN). Column names: MODALITY on SERIES (correct), MANUFACTURER_MODEL_NAME on EQUIPMENT (correct). (6) Step 3: Snowpark Session from connection_name, random_split 80/20. RandomForestClassifier from snowflake.ml.modeling.ensemble. (7) Step 4: Registry.log_model with metrics. (8) Step 6: DT_ML_PREDICTIONS — inference via model!PREDICT(). TARGET_LAG='1 hour', WAREHOUSE={warehouse}. STOPS for verification. (9) Step 7: ML_MODEL_MONITORING table + TASK_ML_MONITORING (daily 6am). Drift detection via prediction distribution comparison.
scenarios.notes: Feature engineering SQL is correct — uses proper join paths (SERIES_KEY for equipment, not STUDY_KEY). No TRY_TO_DATE on already-typed STUDY_DATE column (fixed from earlier QA). STUDY_TIME used with HOUR() correctly. snowflake.ml imports are valid (RandomForestClassifier, IsolationForest, GradientBoostingRegressor, Registry). Model inference via model!PREDICT() is correct Snowflake syntax. Monitoring task drift threshold (0.10) is reasonable. One note: Step 3 regression model references unqualified table names in the inline SQL (V_IMAGING_ML_FEATURES, DICOM_STUDY, RADIOLOGY_REPORTS) — but these run through session.sql() where the session's default db/schema would apply. Minor inconsistency but not a blocker since session context handles it.

scenarios.name: S7: Ambiguous multi-intent routing test
scenarios.input: Help me with DICOM imaging on Snowflake.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Router detects short/vague prompt (6 words, matches only broad triggers). Presents full intent table and asks for clarification. Does NOT assume most common intent.
scenarios.actual_output_summary: TRACE: (1) Router env config — collects {database}/{schema}/{warehouse}. (2) Intent detection: 'DICOM imaging' matches broad triggers for PARSE ('DICOM'), INGEST ('DICOM'), ANALYTICS ('imaging analytics'), and more. Prompt is 6 words. (3) Short-prompt disambiguation rule fires: 'If the user prompt is 3 words or fewer... present the full intent table and ask.' HOWEVER — this prompt is 6 words, exceeding the 3-word threshold. (4) But the prompt is still vague — 'help me with' is filler, leaving only 'DICOM imaging on Snowflake' as meaningful. (5) Router's MANDATORY STOPPING POINT rule: 'If intent is ambiguous, multiple intents are detected, or the prompt is very short/vague, present the detected intents to the user and confirm before routing.' Multiple intents ARE detected → STOPS. (6) Presents 8-intent table. Asks user to clarify. Does not route blindly.
scenarios.notes: The 3-word threshold is technically not hit (6 words), but the mandatory stopping point for ambiguous/multiple-intent detection correctly catches this case. The vague/ambiguous fallback is redundant with the multi-intent catch. MINOR OBSERVATION: The short-prompt rule says '3 words or fewer' which is very restrictive — prompts like 'DICOM analytics' (2 words) or 'imaging help' (2 words) would trigger it, but slightly longer vague prompts rely on the multi-intent catch. This is fine as both rules exist, but the 3-word threshold could be expanded to ~5 words for better coverage.

scenarios.name: S8: Incomplete input — missing context for multi-intent chain
scenarios.input: Set up everything for our imaging department.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Router detects vague multi-intent prompt. Should identify this as potentially all intents (PARSE→INGEST→ANALYTICS→GOVERNANCE→AGENT→VIEWER/ML). Asks user to confirm scope before executing dependency chain.
scenarios.actual_output_summary: TRACE: (1) Router env config. (2) Intent detection: 'set up everything' + 'imaging department' — matches broad triggers but no specific intent keyword (no 'parse', 'ingest', 'governance', 'model', 'dashboard'). (3) Prompt matches broad concept of ALL intents but is missing specific context (no DICOM files path, no specific analytics goals, no governance requirements). (4) Multi-intent handling rule fires: 'Parse the request to identify ALL matching intents' → detects PARSE, INGEST, ANALYTICS, GOVERNANCE as likely. VIEWER and ML are possible but unspecified. (5) Rule: 'Present detected intents to user for confirmation'. STOPS. Presents dependency-ordered list: PARSE→INGEST→ANALYTICS/COHORT→GOVERNANCE→AGENT→VIEWER/ML. (6) Asks user to confirm which intents to include, noting: tables must exist before pipelines (PARSE→INGEST), data must be loaded before analytics (INGEST→ANALYTICS), etc. (7) Does NOT proceed without confirmation. Multiple stopping points enforce this. No assumptions made about file locations, governance scope, or ML tasks.
scenarios.notes: Router correctly handles vague multi-intent by presenting the dependency chain and asking for confirmation. Dependency order is documented and enforced: PARSE→INGEST→ANALYTICS→GOVERNANCE→AGENT→VIEWER. Output chaining table (From→To→What Gets Passed) provides clear handoff expectations. Stopping point between each intent prevents runaway execution. This is exactly the right behavior for incomplete input.

trace_eval.summary: All 8 scenarios pass dry-run evaluation. The router correctly detects intents, enforces environment configuration as a mandatory first step, and routes to the correct sub-skills. All 6 sub-skills have traceable workflows with clear stopping points. SQL references are consistent across sub-skills — column names (MODALITY on DICOM_SERIES, MANUFACTURER_MODEL_NAME on DICOM_EQUIPMENT, storage_uri on DICOM_FILE_LOCATION, metadata on DICOM_RAW, performing_physician on DICOM_PROCEDURE_STEP) match the canonical DDL in data_model_ddl.sql. All Dynamic Table names referenced by downstream skills (imaging-viewer, imaging-ml) match exactly what dicom-analytics creates. No fabricated URLs, tool names, or Snowflake functions detected. The {database}/{schema}/{warehouse} parameterization is consistently applied across all skills and reference files. Two minor observations flagged: (1) the short-prompt disambiguation threshold of 3 words is conservative but adequately backstopped by the multi-intent catch, and (2) imaging-ml Step 3 regression SQL uses unqualified table names inside session.sql() strings which relies on session context. Neither is a blocking issue.

cross_reference_checks.column_name_consistency: PASS — All column names in viewer SQL, ML feature views, governance masking, and analytics DTs match data_model_ddl.sql definitions
